title: Grove's Tokenized Treasury Instances disable every optional capability of the venue and enable only the path they need
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.14.1.4.1 and A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.14.2.4.1 give both Tokenized Treasury Instances a verbatim-identical *Instance Configuration Parameters* block:

- Max Swap Size: 50,000,000 USD
- Staleness Threshold: seven (7) days
- Fees: 0
- Credit Token Deposits: **Disabled**
- Credit Token Withdrawals: **Disabled**
- Stablecoin Swaps: **Disabled**

Three of six parameters exist only to switch functionality off. That tells us the underlying Basin/Tokenized Treasury contracts are general — they support credit token deposits and withdrawals and stablecoin swaps — and that Grove has chosen to enable none of it.

This is default-deny applied to contract capability rather than to permissions. Code that is deployed but disabled cannot be exploited through this Instance, so disabling reduces the attack surface to the one flow the Instance actually needs. It also means that a bug in the swap path or the credit-token path is not Grove's problem here, which materially narrows what the pending risk review has to cover.

Note the interaction with the Max Swap Size of 50,000,000 USD: a swap limit is configured on an Instance where Stablecoin Swaps are Disabled. The limit is inert while the flag stays off, so enabling the flag later would silently activate a 50,000,000 allowance that no one approved in the context of live swaps. Disabled-but-parameterized capabilities are a latent authorization — the safe reading is that turning a flag on requires re-reviewing every parameter that flag governs, not just the flag.
description: Credit Token Deposits, Credit Token Withdrawals and Stablecoin Swaps are all Disabled with Fees 0 on both JTRSY and BUIDL, narrowing the attack surface to the single authorized flow.
